article_title: Shanghai Startup Zhongqi Wuliang Unveils Server-Rack Neutral-Atom Quantum Computer at WAIC 2026
summary: Approved with corrections: strong, well-sourced submission, but one subordinate paragraph misattributes prior-generation systems (Hanyuan-1, Hanyuan-2) to the subject company when the cited source credits Hanyuan-1 to a different company (Zhongke Kuyuan).

findings.message: Misattributed corporate history: Hanyuan-1 and Hanyuan-2 credited to Zhongqi Wuliang, but source credits Hanyuan-1 to a different company.
findings.details: body_markdown states 'Zhongqi Wuliang previously built Hanyuan-1... followed by Hanyuan-2...' The cited Quantum Computing Report snapshot (source-0.html.gz) explicitly states 'Hanyuan-1 (October 2025): Developed by Zhongke Kuyuan, this 100-qubit, room-temperature neutral-atom system...' -- a different company than Zhongqi Wuliang. The source credits only Qinghe No. 1 to Zhongqi Wuliang in that list. Confined to a subordinate paragraph in 'What We Know'; not in headline, summary, or lead. Addressed via corrections record per APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS verdict.

content_preview.title: Shanghai Startup Zhongqi Wuliang Unveils Server-Rack Neutral-Atom Quantum Computer at WAIC 2026
content_preview.summary: Zhongqi Wuliang showed Qinghe No. 1, a neutral-atom quantum computer built to fit a standard data-center rack, at WAIC 2026 in Shanghai.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

A Shanghai quantum computing startup has shown off a machine designed to look and fit like ordinary data-center equipment rather than laboratory apparatus. At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) 2026 in Shanghai, [Zhongqi Wuliang](https://quantumcomputingreport.com/zhongqi-wuliang-unveils-server-rack-neutral-atom-quantum-computer-at-waic-2026/) formally unveiled Qinghe No. 1, a neutral-atom quantum computer engineered to fit directly into a standard data-center serve...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece using the site's Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure. Neutral, non-sensational tone throughout; no AI self-reference. Word count (518) is within the News category range (400-1200). Attribution phrasing ('according to Quantum Computing Report', 'The Quantum Insider explained...') is used consistently and correctly links claims to their source outlet.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both cited sources were fetched successfully by chief:review (HTTP 200, no errors, archive_fallback: false) and their gzip snapshots were read in full from disk at sources/2026-07/shanghai-startup-zhongqi-wuliang-unveils-server-rack-neutral-atom-quantum-computer-at-waic-2026/. Integrity was confirmed by decompressing each file and re-hashing: source-0.html.gz -> sha256 9efa2d236fc2f438f5e9ee9b048e24dd111b3c2b312ea6a2413466a157e2d1be (matches manifest); source-1.html.gz -> sha256 a6514ac4d2ea846d3aeaf0f529c2dd14a5e463d06bb5b83daa712559c4043dcd (matches manifest). No WebFetch fallback was needed. Findings per source: (1) source-0.html.gz (Quantum Computing Report, 'Zhongqi Wuliang Unveils Server-Rack Neutral-Atom Quantum Computer at WAIC 2026') confirms: the WAIC 2026 Shanghai venue and formal unveiling of Qinghe No. 1; the company's spin-out from CAS SIOM and founding by Lu Xudong; the optical-tweezer/laser-cooling/Rydberg-blockade-gate technical description (verified near-verbatim); the Xuanxiang Technology supply-chain detail verbatim; the Google Quantum AI Boulder, Colorado neutral-atom program claim verbatim; and the unverified/no-peer-reviewed-metrics caveat verbatim. It does NOT confirm the article's claim that Zhongqi Wuliang built Hanyuan-1 and Hanyuan-2 -- see Findings below. (2) source-1.html.gz (The Quantum Insider, 'Shanghai Startup Unveils Data Center-Ready Quantum Computer at WAIC 2026') confirms: the 2025 founding date and CAS SIOM incubation verbatim; the direct quote 'the first quantum computer concept designed in a standard server form factor for direct installation in existing data center racks' verbatim, correctly attributed via Pandaily; the five-year commercialization horizon claim verbatim; the 'individual atoms held in place by laser light' / 'every atom is naturally identical... avoids manufacturing variations' explanation verbatim; and the framing of neutral atoms alongside superconducting and trapped-ion approaches verbatim. Every direct quote in the article appears verbatim in its cited snapshot. No hallucinated quotes were found. Both outlets are credible, on-topic trade publications (Quantum Computing Report and The Quantum Insider) appropriate for this beat.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: One verified misattribution: the body_markdown paragraph 'Qinghe No. 1 is not the company's first system. Quantum Computing Report reports that Zhongqi Wuliang previously built Hanyuan-1... followed by Hanyuan-2...' is not supported by the cited source. The Quantum Computing Report snapshot explicitly attributes Hanyuan-1 to a DIFFERENT company: 'Hanyuan-1 (October 2025): Developed by Zhongke Kuyuan, this 100-qubit, room-temperature neutral-atom system...' (verified in both the extracted text and the raw HTML via grep). The source presents Hanyuan-1, Hanyuan-2, and Qinghe No. 1 as three separate milestones in 'China's Accelerating Neutral-Atom Roadmap' (a regional/industry-wide framing), explicitly crediting only Qinghe No. 1 to Zhongqi Wuliang ('Qinghe No. 1 (July 2026): Zhongqi Wuliang's single-rack form factor...'). Hanyuan-2's developer is not explicitly named in the source, but its adjacency to Hanyuan-1 in the same bullet list (shared naming convention, no re-attribution to Zhongqi Wuliang) does not support crediting it to Zhongqi Wuliang either. This is a subordinate claim confined to one paragraph in the 'What We Know' section -- it does not appear in the headline, summary, or Overview lead, all of which are independently well-sourced. Every other specific, number, name, date, and direct quote in the article was individually checked against the snapshots and confirmed accurate.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Appropriately hedges unverified company claims (e.g., 'though it has not disclosed specific technical milestones', 'remains unverified outside the company's own claims'). No sensationalism or editorializing.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior coverage of Zhongqi Wuliang, Qinghe No. 1, and this WAIC 2026 unveiling -- no match found. Existing neutral-atom quantum computing coverage in the archive (e.g., 2026-03 QuEra/Microsoft/Pasqal error-correction piece, 2026-05 ETH Zurich swap-gate fidelity piece, 2026-07 Oratomic funding piece) covers different companies, different events, and different angles. This is a genuinely new topic with no duplicate or substantial overlap.
concerns: The article states Zhongqi Wuliang 'previously built Hanyuan-1... followed by Hanyuan-2', but the cited Quantum Computing Report source explicitly attributes Hanyuan-1 to a different company, Zhongke Kuyuan, and does not attribute Hanyuan-2 to Zhongqi Wuliang either. This is a misattribution of corporate history, confined to one subordinate paragraph outside the headline/summary/lead.
recommendations: File alongside publication a corrections record clarifying that Hanyuan-1 and Hanyuan-2 were not established by the source as Zhongqi Wuliang products, and that the source instead credits Hanyuan-1 to Zhongke Kuyuan.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced News piece on a genuinely new topic. All technical description, direct quotes, founding details, and forward-looking caveats were individually verified against both source snapshots and hold up. One subordinate paragraph misattributes two prior-generation systems (Hanyuan-1, Hanyuan-2) to the subject company when the cited source credits Hanyuan-1 to a different company (Zhongke Kuyuan) and does not credit Hanyuan-2 to Zhongqi Wuliang at all. Because this error sits outside the headline/summary/lead and is a single coherent conflation rather than a pattern of unrelated fabrications, it is honestly correctable with one public corrections note. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
